stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: A diode passes current one way only. Sweep the DC source $E$ from negative to positive and watch the operating point $(V_D,\,I)$ crawl along the characteristic. Reach both a reverse setting ($E < 0$) and a forward setting well past the knee ($E > 1\,\text{V}$) to advance.
stages.concept: Shockley: $I = I_S\,(e^{V_D/V_T} - 1)$. Below the threshold $V_{th} \approx 0.6\,\text{V}$ current is essentially zero — the diode blocks. Above threshold, current climbs almost exponentially — the diode conducts. Reverse bias ($V_D < 0$): only a tiny leakage.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: The source is now AC: $V_{in}(t) = V_p \sin(2\pi f t)$. Change $V_p$ and watch the output $V_R$ (green) — the diode chops off the negative half and the small $V_{th}$ slice. Move the slider at least twice to advance.
stages.concept: Half-wave rectification: $V_R(t) = \max(0,\,V_{in}(t) - V_{th})$. Only positive half-cycles above $V_{th}$ pass. The negative half-cycle is blocked entirely.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The scope shows a target output waveform (orange) for the same AC input. Pick the diode topology that produces it. Peek reveals the answer for $1.5\,\text{s}$.
stages.concept: Topology decides the shape. Single forward diode → half-wave (positive humps). Reversed diode → clips to the negative half (negative humps). Bridge of 4 diodes → both half-cycles flipped positive (full-wave).

labels.tip1: sweep E through zero · reverse blocks, forward conducts past V_th
labels.tip2: V_p sets amplitude · the diode always chops at V_th
labels.tip3: match the target waveform shape to the topology

1.1: Slide E below zero — nothing conducts (I ≈ 0). That's reverse bias.
1.2: Now slide E past +0.6 V — current suddenly climbs. The knee is V_th.
1.3: You need one visit at E < 0 AND one at E > 1 V to advance.

2.1: V_p is the peak of the AC input (dashed). V_R (solid) is what survives.
2.2: Try V_p = 1 V — the output is tiny (V_th eats most of it). Then V_p = 5 V — most of the top half-cycle passes.
2.3: The negative half is always zero. That's what 'half-wave' means.

3.1: Positive humps only → single forward diode. Negative humps only → reversed diode.
3.2: All humps positive (no gap between them) → 4-diode bridge. Both halves are flipped up.
3.3: Peek shows the answer directly for 1.5 s.
